hypothesis: The locked ACCDB does not export the CAESAR material-library mean thermal-expansion/derived thermal-strain authority as a separate pipe-element field. A complete read-only table/column inventory plus input-only candidate-table inspection can prove the export boundary without using InputXML or benchmark output fitting.

authoritySources.document: CAESAR II User's Guide Version 14 - Elements (Input Export Options)
authoritySources.authorityStatement: INPUT_BASIC_ELEMENT_DATA exports TEMP_EXP_C1 through C9 as a thermal-expansion-coefficient-or-temperature input field, plus material and elastic-modulus fields.

authoritySources.document: CAESAR II User's Guide Version 14 - Thermal Expansion
authoritySources.authorityStatement: Thermal Expansion is a read-only derived thermal strain corresponding to entered operating temperature when material expansion data are available.

authoritySources.document: CAESAR II User's Guide Version 14 - Thermal Bowing
authoritySources.authorityStatement: For B31.1/B31.3, mean thermal expansion is referenced to 70 F / 21 C and CAESAR material-library values are interpolated from code material data.
Piping Code ID 53 maps to ASME B31.3-2022 with B31J-2017.

authoritySources.document: CAESAR II User's Guide Version 14 - Reducers (Input Export Options)
authoritySources.authorityStatement: INPUT_REDUCERS.ALPHA is reducer transition slope, not thermal expansion.

authoritySources.document: CAESAR II User's Guide Version 14 - Auxiliary Element Data
authoritySources.authorityStatement: Alpha:h, Alpha:fab and Alpha:gw are DNV-2017 auxiliary material/code fields, not pipe thermal-expansion coefficients.

authoritySources.document: CAESAR II User's Guide Version 14 - Material Database Editor
authoritySources.authorityStatement: Delivered physical-property authority is read from the supplied material database; user modifications are stored in a secondary UMD database.

predictedSignature: Inventory every ACCDB table and column through read-only ACE schema metadata; do not read alternate model formats.
Confirm the locked ACCDB SHA-256 before inventory.
Resolve whether TEMP_EXP_C1 is temperature or direct expansion input for this locked job from the actual value rather than from the column name alone.
Disambiguate unrelated ALPHA/COEFF fields by their owning CAESAR table/mechanic.

If no separate exported pipe field carries the material-library mean expansion coefficient or resulting thermal strain, require an independently sourced, versioned profile authority rather than a benchmark-fitted constant.
I009's ~12.23199e-6/K implied coefficient remains diagnostic-only and is not promoted by this inventory.
mechanicsDelta: None. Schema/input-authority evidence only; no solver, profile, tolerance, or benchmark-reference changes.
decisionReason: The exact-head locked-data audit proves the relevant export boundary. For BM4_NL, TEMP_EXP_C1 is 120 C on the A106 Grade B source elements, while the ACCDB contains no separate pipe-element field for CAESAR's material-library mean CTE or the read-only derived thermal strain. The only literal THERM_EXP_COEFF belongs to an empty API-650 nozzle table; INPUT_REDUCERS.ALPHA is geometric reducer slope; INPUT_ALLOWABLES ALPHA fields are code-specific non-thermal fields; no Bourdon column exists. Therefore the reusable solver must obtain the 21->120 C B31.3-2022 A106 Grade B expansion authority from a versioned CAESAR/ASME material authority outside the locked ACCDB and fail closed if that provenance is absent. This finding authorizes no numeric CTE change and does not promote the I009/I010 benchmark-inferred coefficient.
